text:
Like shoots whose fresh adornments
a freezing north wind destroys in bloom,
so fell the child heroes
before the invader's bullets.


Fleeting as a dream, the span
of their ideal childhood
was; but Glory, immortal mother,
lulled them in her lap.


Soon the beloved homeland
needed their lives,
and one after another, life
they smilingly gave her.


On the laughing hill
of the Forest, one following another,
they fell, with the divine
majesty of a young god.


Who, after hearing tell
of such pious offering,
would deny the Homeland
the blood she gave him?


Childhood that found a Calvary
at life's dawn:
may the tricolor flag
serve you as a shroud.


And may heaven and earth
sing your deeds without cease,
the condor of the mountains
and the waves of the sea…

translation.title: The Child Heroes of Chapultepec
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the patriotic elegy, Chapultepec, and the tricolor flag as a shroud.
